source.title: Persona Features Control Emergent Misalignment
source.authors: Miles Wang; Tom Dupré la Tour; Olivia Watkins; Aleksandar Makelov; Ryan A. Chi; Samuel Miserendino; Johannes Heidecke; Tejal Patwardhan; Daniel P. Mossing

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper cites the refusal-direction study in related work but its own experiments concern emergent misalignment, not refusal. Its interventions do not test refusal on harmful requests or refusal of harmless requests.
record.gate_note: The paper mentions prior work on one-dimensional refusal control but reports no new refusal-direction result. Its own SAE steering results concern misalignment; those are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version. The cited results from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper cites Arditi et al. only as background: one-dimensional control of refusal in related work and Section 3.1. Its experiments steer SAE latents to change emergent misalignment in GPT-4o. It never computes the harmful-minus-harmless direction, never ablates or adds a refusal direction, and never measures refusal of harmful prompts as a function of a direction. The Figure 11 'Harmful non-refusal' category is a latent-steering misalignment profile, not a refusal-direction test.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors also show emergent misalignment arises under RL in o3-mini and in helpful-only models, and that it grows with model size. They also show the toxic-persona latent can detect misalignment early, for example at 5% incorrect data.
record.recipe_differences: The paper ranks SAE features by activation changes after fine-tuning and steers their decoder directions; it does not use the harmful-minus-harmless instruction mean-difference refusal direction or test refusal.
record.method_sensitivity: Steering strength is adapted to keep incoherence ≤ 10%.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE latent #10 ('toxic persona') steers emergent misalignment: positive steering raises misalignment in GPT-4o and negative steering suppresses it in fine-tuned misaligned models. Latent #-1 ('assistant persona') re-aligns misaligned models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Emergent misalignment is mediated by a small set of persona directions found by SAE model-diffing.

fits_no_version.finding: Latent #10 activates strongly on persona jailbreak prompts (AUROC 0.96 vs benign prompts) (Appendix D.5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Persona jailbreaks activate a toxic-persona feature, which is distinct from the refusal direction.

record.problems: No direct evidence on refusal or the refusal direction. The steering values for these results are presented in figures without numerical values in the text; general capability preservation is not tested.

untested.parts: Diff-in-means refusal direction; its ablation or addition; refusal rates; capability preservation.
Jailbreaks suppressing the refusal direction; adversarial training. The study shows only that persona jailbreaks activate a toxic-persona latent, which is not the refusal direction.
Multi-dimensional or cone structure of refusal.
Harmfulness encoding vs. the refusal decision.
Transfer across languages, variants, or base-to-instruct. The SAE is trained on the base model and applied to the chat model, but for misalignment features, not refusal.
Training dependence of the refusal direction. Helpful-only models are studied, but for misalignment, not refusal-direction existence.
Refusal direction in reasoning models. o3-mini is studied only for emergent misalignment under RL.

record.verdict_notes: Refusal appears only as a cited prior result (Arditi et al.) and as a grader category. Treat as cites_only / T6 for refusal_direction.

versions.untested_parts: The harmful-minus-harmless instruction difference direction, its ablation or addition, refusal behavior, and preservation of other capabilities.
Weight-edit ablation or abliteration and its effect on refusal in released models.
Whether attacks suppress the refusal direction or training against its ablation improves robustness.
Whether refusal is represented by an affine structure, cone, or multiple directions.
Whether harmfulness judgment is encoded separately from the refusal decision.
Transfer of a refusal direction across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models.
How refusal-training choices determine whether a removable refusal direction exists.
Whether the refusal-direction claim holds in reasoning models.

rows.subject: GPT-4o
rows.operation_detail: Steered token activations in the SAE layer positively along latent #10, called the toxic persona latent.

conditions.value: positive; strength selected subject to incoherence ≤ 10%

rows.note: The text says positive steering with this latent causes misalignment in the original GPT-4o model. This is misalignment, not refusal.
rows.check: Linked correctly to no version. Measures misalignment under SAE latent #10 steering, not refusal. Fig. 9 gives 57% overall misalignment for #10 positive steering (Fig. 11), so the value can be read rather than 'figure only'. Baseline: original GPT-4o, near 0%.

rows.subject: GPT-4o fine-tuned on incorrect datasets
rows.operation_detail: Steered token activations in the SAE layer negatively along latent #10, called the toxic persona latent.

conditions.value: negative; strength selected subject to incoherence ≤ 10%

rows.note: The text says negative steering suppresses misalignment in misaligned fine-tuned models; it does not say the effect removes all misalignment.
rows.check: Linked correctly to no version. Negative steering suppresses misalignment in fine-tuned models; the value is figure-only. Not a refusal measure.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
